study: Separate nonlinear tire forces from sliced-cylinder contact geometry in PhysX
sequence: Freeze and record the current contact-reward/control checkpoint, including failures; a perfect baseline is not required for a contact-model diagnostic.
Validate each new contact representation on a single wheel before the full robot.
Replay one declared frozen policy under each contact-model arm at nominal mu0.7.
After the model comparisons and coupling checks, train separate matched-budget policies under the declared contact models.
Validate within each model and transfer between models; extend friction evaluation after nominal results are recorded.
main_system: TRON1 WF driven two-wheel articulation, traj_4

initial_diagnostic_policy.selection_reason: Declared existing tracking baseline; does not satisfy continuous-support acceptance.

primary_geometry_levels.definition: Existing authored wheel collision geometry, audited from the USD; do not assume an ideal analytic cylinder if its collider is a convex approximation.
Nine contiguous, coaxial cylinder colliders with equal radius and total axial width matched to the declared cylinder envelope.
primary_geometry_levels.purpose: Study contact representation and manifold changes with a matched envelope.
primary_geometry_levels.required_additional_control: If the authored wheel is not an analytic cylinder, include one unsliced analytic cylinder with the same declared envelope.

primary_force_levels.definition: An explicitly declared nonlinear longitudinal/lateral tire-force law using wheel contact kinematics and measured normal load.

profiled_or_crowned_slices.definition: Declare a radius-versus-axial-position profile for each slice.

measurements: Core and whole-trajectory XY error, speed retention and intended reference-beta error
Body heading, velocity direction and each wheel rolling-plane heading
Per-wheel hub angle and actual contact-point longitudinal/lateral velocity
Physical-substep normal and tangential forces, impulses and support gaps
Aggregate friction utilization with its patch-versus-point limitations
Support-gap onset relative to control updates and stance-leg target changes
Body angular high-frequency motion and normal-force discontinuities

car_and_human_extensions.original_scale_car: Separate source/surrogate study; preserve clock and plant-identification caveats from the previous measured protocol.
car_and_human_extensions.human_motion_prior: Assess GMR/AMP posture, load-transfer and support-timing value after the tire/contact comparison is defined; do not infer benefit from slicing alone.
